subject: BlueSpring follow-up: IR timelines, SOC 2 evidence, and next steps
messages:
From: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
To: elena.moreno@bluespringhealth.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: BlueSpring follow-up: IR timelines, SOC 2 evidence, and next steps

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Scope we discussed: customer-facing patient search and summary features that will send de-identified embeddings to Redwood Hosted inference.
- Security priorities you called out: SOC 2 Type II proof, breach notification timelines (HIPAA/PII escalation), BCP/DR evidence for on-call/responsibility mapping, and vendor questionnaire kickoff.

Suggested next steps: 
1) I’ll share our most recent SOC 2 Type II report + a concise IR playbook and BCP/DR summary for your security team to review (attached).
2) If helpful, we can map the breach-notification timeline to BlueSpring’s required windows (48/72 hours) and document how Redwood would trigger customer notification and law/regulator communication.
3) Can you share the vendor security questionnaire (or a link to the procurement portal)? We’ll begin filling it out and propose a single point-of-contact for evidence.

Action items: (a) I’ll attach the baseline artifacts by EOD, (b) Ben will help with any technical evidence (network diagrams, backup runbooks), and (c) Marissa will coordinate a short follow-up call with your security ops to walk through any gaps.

Would next Wednesday (May 27) at 10am PT work for a 30-minute follow-up with your security and IT Ops?

Thanks — talk soon.

— Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147
[Attachment stubs will follow in a separate email]
From: elena.moreno@bluespringhealth.com
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: itops@bluespringhealth.com, security_ops@bluespringhealth.com, procurement@bluespringhealth.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 18:54:12 -0400
Subject: Re: BlueSpring follow-up: IR timelines, SOC 2 evidence, and next steps

Thanks, Soojin — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifying questions before we loop in our procurement team formally: 

1) SOC 2: Can you confirm the report covers the hosted inference environment (multi-tenant) and list the subservice organizations, if any? We’ll need the scope and the report date.
2) Breach notification: Our policy requires preliminary notification to our security team within 24 hours of detection and regulated customer notification within 72 hours for incidents involving PHI. Can Redwood commit to a 24-hour detection notification to BlueSpring for confirmed incidents and provide a sample timeline in your IR playbook?
3) IR evidence: examples we expect are timeline-of-events templates, sample post-incident communication, and proof of periodic DR tabletop exercises for the last 12 months.

We’ll attach a copy of our vendor questionnaire in a follow-up email (procurement will send that). For now, please send the SOC 2 and IR artifacts you mentioned so our security team can start their internal review.

Elena Moreno
Head of Security, BlueSpring Health
elena.moreno@bluespringhealth.com

Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueSpring follow-up: IR timelines, SOC 2 evidence, and next steps

Sooj — quick note on artifacts. I’ve pulled the latest items: 
- SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2024.pdf (covers Redwood Hosted API; scope includes inference service, identity management, and log retention subprocesses).
- IR_Playbook_v1.pdf (contains detection workflow, escalation contacts, notification templates, and sample timelines; redacted internal emails for customer-facing examples).
- BCP_DR_Summary.xlsx (table with last 12 months of tabletop exercises, RTO/RPO targets, and primary DR contacts).

I recommend we redact a couple of internal IPs (network VLAN ids) before sending the SOC report publicly; otherwise we can mark them as available under NDA/secure portal. I’ll prepare the redacted versions and flag any items that require procurement access.

Also, if they need 24-hour detection notification commitment in writing, we should confirm with Legal. I’ll ping Legal for an acceptable commitment language draft and include it in the follow-up mail.

— Ben
